parsed.explanation: The parent regime creates real border and document exposure: X passports are no longer issued, entry officers are instructed to scrutinise sex discrepancies and may pursue a permanent fraud finding, and national facilities and custody policies are hostile. Within this state, however, there is no bathroom ban, public-accommodation discrimination based on gender identity has been prohibited since 2003, single-occupancy facilities are gender-neutral, hate-crime law covers gender identity, and a shield law protects interstate travellers seeking care. No local police targeting or facility exclusion is documented. The protections are longstanding statutes rather than recently proven enforcement outcomes, and the hostile parent border/custody layer remains, so it sits materially above the national average but below the strongest low-risk cases.
